subject: Request: runtime telemetry visibility exception & redline coordination
messages:
From: Tom Waller <twaller@medicore.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Medicore Legal <legal@medicore.com>, Baker & Finch <contracts@bakerfinch.com>
Date: 2027-09-15 08:14 AM -0700
Subject: DPA redline - runtime telemetry visibility

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our legal team attached a first-pass redline to the DPA focused on telemetry and runtime visibility: they want assurance that any inference-level telemetry exported to Redwood or third parties will be limited to non-identifying metadata and cannot be used to reconstitute inputs. They also requested an explicit subprocessor restriction for any analytics vendors that might receive request-level traces.

I'm attaching their redline for your team to review (medicore_dpa_redline_v1.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the proposed limitation on telemetry exports or propose language that achieves equivalent risk reduction while preserving observability for debugging production issues?

Appreciate a turnaround this week if possible — our procurement is aiming to finalize in the next 10 days.

Cheers,
Tom
Head of Platform Ops, Medicore
(attachment: medicore_dpa_redline_v1.pdf)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15 10:02 AM -0700
Subject: FW: DPA redline - runtime telemetry visibility — need product/security/legal take

Team —

Forwarding Medicore's DPA redline. High level: they want a hard restriction that prevents request-level traces from being exported to any analytics/subprocessor that could re-identify inputs. They also included a clause requiring prior written consent for any new telemetry subprocessor.

Quick asks:
- Olga: legal suggested text? Anything obviously unacceptable from a contracting perspective?
- Irene: does security see a technical problem with locking telemetry to coarse aggregates only? Any controls we can offer (e.g., encryption-at-rest with HSM, retention windows, access controls) that would be acceptable to them?
- Karthik: product/ops — what is the production/debugging impact if we restrict request-level traces to internal-only (no export to analytics vendors)? What tradeoffs for latency-debugging and root-cause analysis?

I've attached a working response with tracked changes to start (redwood_response_track_changes.docx). If we can get internal sign-off by EOD tomorrow I will propose a compromise to Medicore and ask for a short procurement extension.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_response_track_changes.docx)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15 15:24 PM -0700
Subject: RE: FW: DPA redline - runtime telemetry visibility — need product/security/legal take

Vanessa / team —

I reviewed Medicore's redline. High-level legal stance: the proposed absolute ban on exporting request-level traces to any subprocessor is very restrictive and will block our ability to offer managed analytics for performance troubleshooting. Contractually, we can offer tight constraints instead of a full ban:

- Define "request-level trace" and narrow it to include only sequence identifiers, timing, and non-payload metadata; exclude full prompt/response content.
- Allow exports to an "allowed analytics subprocessor list" that we will maintain and provide to Medicore, with prior notice for changes and a right to object for bona fide security/privacy reasons (short review window, e.g., 10 business days).
- Commit to encryption of traces at rest and to retention windows (e.g., 30 days default, negotiable).

I've marked specific phrasing in the response doc and added suggested counter-language. Note: we should keep an internal fallback if a customer insists on zero export — we can offer a private deployment or dedicated mode (no third-party analytics) but that'll have pricing/operations implications.

—Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-16 09:11 AM -0700
Subject: RE: FW: DPA redline - runtime telemetry visibility — need product/security/legal take

Thanks for the ping. Security perspective: Medicore's concern about re-identification is legitimate. Technical options we can offer:

- Masking and tokenization pipeline: strip or hash any inbound PII fields before traces are logged.
- Field-level redaction for request/response payloads; only retain numeric timing/latency fields and event-type enums in shared telemetry.
- Short retention windows with automated purge (configurable per-customer; default 30d).
- HSM-backed KMS for telemetry encryption keys and strict RBAC to limit who can decrypt traces.
- Audit logging for any access to traces, exposed in Console for Medicore's auditors.

Operational impact: the masking/tokenization step adds negligible latency if done at edge. However, full removal of request-level traces from analytics vendors will impair our ability to proactively detect certain performance regressions that require request-level context; we can mitigate with sampling (e.g., 0.1% request-level traces available to internal SRE and on-request exports with Medicore consent).

If legal accepts the "allowed analytics subprocessor list + retention + masking" approach, security can sign off with the above controls documented in a runbook. Happy to draft the technical annex.

—Irene
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-16 14:28 PM -0700
Subject: RE: FW: DPA redline - runtime telemetry visibility — need product/security/legal take

Quick product assessment:

- Full ban on request-level exports: If Medicore insists, we can support by scoping them to private deployment or Dedicated with analytics disabled — this reduces our ability to provide managed SLO alerting and raises cost (we'll need to keep more in-house signals).
- Compromise path: provide masked/sampled request traces to a named analytics vendor list. Implement a per-customer toggle for "request-level export" with default off. For debugging, offer a time-limited enable by request (with Medicore approval) and capture an auditor-visible justification.
- Work needed: config UI for per-customer export toggles, docs for the runbook, and an update to onboarding checklist. Estimated effort: 3 sprint cycles across infra + console (around 6 weeks) to ship the toggle + masking in a hardened way. Short-term mitigation: we can offer Medicore a support-level playbook to run captures on-demand (SRE-assisted) while we negotiate.

Recommendation: accept Olga/Irene language that narrows definitions, add a clause for an allowed analytics list, offer a 30-day retention and sampling at 0.1% for proactive detection, and include an option for time-limited diagnostic exports subject to Medicore's written consent. This balances their privacy ask and our operational needs.

—Karthik (Product)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Waller <twaller@medicore.com>, Medicore Legal <legal@medicore.com>, Baker & Finch <contracts@bakerfinch.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18 16:02 PM -0700
Subject: RE: DPA redline - runtime telemetry visibility 

Tom —

Thanks for the redline and patience while we reviewed internally. We've proposed an alternative that we believe addresses Medicore's re-identification concerns while keeping necessary operational observability:

1) Narrow the definition of "request-level trace" to exclude full prompt/response payloads and to include only timing, routing, and non-payload enums.
2) Allow telemetry exports only to a named "allowed analytics subprocessor list" (we'll provide the list and notify you prior to any additions; you have a 10-business-day review window to raise objections).
3) Default retention for shared telemetry = 30 days; we will purge on request and provide audit logs of access.
4) Masking/tokenization applied at edge; sampling of 0.1% request-level traces retained for proactive detection and for time-limited diagnostic captures with Medicore's written consent.

If Medicore needs a zero-export option, we can propose Dedicated/Private deployment pricing that disables third-party analytics. I've attached our proposed tracked-changes response for your team to review. Can you confirm whether the above is acceptable or if Medicore will require further tightening? If you need more time to review, please let us know and we can extend the procurement window by a week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood_response_track_changes.docx)
